newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES SOFTER.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market was indicated liquid on Monday with short-term trading rates quoted softer on the whole, dealers said.
They said the market was in surplus of Z$90.2 million over the weekend with a further Z$68.8 million inflow expected on Monday, resulting from the maturity of a three-year government stock issue.
The Reserve Bank had however already come into the market offering Z$150 million worth of treasury bills to mop up the excess cash, the dealers added.
Meanwhile, discount houses were selling 91-day treasury bills in the secondary market at 17.55 percent from Friday's 17.50 to 18.50 percentage range while call money eased to 18 from 19 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were being bought at 18.50 percent from between 18 and 19.50 percent and sold at 18.25 percent after previously fluctuating between 18.35 percent and 18.75 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 18.25 and 18 percent (buying and selling respectively).
